artifacts.title: Doty v. Nashville Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: Ms. Doty and 21 others filed charges against a Nashville Presbytery teaching elder first with his congregation's Session (wrong court), then with Nashville Presbytery; Presbytery declined to indict and treated the matter as a report under BCO 31-2 rather than charges. The SJC dismissed the complaint as judicially out of order (11-9-2-2) on the ground that Doty lacked standing under BCO 43-1 as a non-member of Nashville Presbytery; a significant dissent argued that her filing of charges gave her standing under prior precedent (Lyons, Ruff, Fordice).

artifacts.synopsis: Fordice complained that Pacific Northwest Presbytery erred by allowing TE Nathan Lewis to confess under BCO 38-1 and closing the matter without adequate process, after its own investigative committee had found a strong presumption of guilt on 18 allegations. The SJC unanimously sustained the complaint and remanded the case to PNW, finding that while use of BCO 38-1 was not itself error, the approved statement of facts was not 'full' as required because it failed to correlate with the underlying allegations.

The SJC found most responses satisfactory, but found one response unsatisfactory (regarding charges against a TE that were not properly processed under BCO 32-2), and noted an additional exception of substance regarding improper divestiture under BCO 46-8.

artifacts.title: Thompson v. South Florida Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: The SJC sustained Thompson's complaint, finding that the Granada Session's judicial commission procedurally erred in imposing excommunication for contumacy before trial because Thompson's behavior did not constitute the immediately censurable kind of contumacy under BCO 32-6.b, and that failing to reach a BCO 38-1 agreement should have led to a trial rather than a pre-trial judgment; the SJC annulled the excommunication and restored the matter to its pre-judgment status as of June 26, 2015.

artifacts.synopsis: Steven Hahn challenged Philadelphia Metro West Presbytery's handling of complaints arising from Christ the King's restriction on his attendance while he sought a psychiatric evaluation. The SJC denied the complaint, holding that the Session's action was pastoral guidance rather than judicial censure and that no clear error was shown in the lower courts' judgment.

artifacts.synopsis: The SJC denied a complaint by Kirk Lyons challenging Western Carolina Presbytery's dismissal of charges he filed against TE Craig Bulkeley, finding no clear error in the presbytery's determination that grounds existed under BCO 31-8, 34-2, and 32-20 to decline the charges, though the SJC noted the presbytery erred (non-prejudicially) in denying Lyons standing, since filing BCO 32-2 charges brought him under the court's jurisdiction.

artifacts.title: McNeil v. Chesapeake Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: McNeil complained that Chesapeake Presbytery erred in denying his complaint against the Session's refusal to receive his charges against his wife after the Session had already censured him for abusive behavior; the SJC denied the complaint, applying a standard of great deference to the lower court and finding no clear procedural error.

artifacts.synopsis: Matt Ruff complained that Nashville Presbytery failed to conduct an adequate BCO 31-2 investigation and to find a strong presumption of guilt against TE George Grant; the SJC sustained both complaints and remanded, finding the investigation record was incomplete and internally inconsistent, and that conduct described by the Presbytery's own Shepherding Committee as 'sin' required an explanation as to why no strong presumption of guilt existed.

artifacts.synopsis: TE Martin Payne and related complainants challenged Western Carolina Presbytery's BCO 31-2 investigation of accusations concerning TE Craig Bulkeley and its conclusion that no strong presumption of guilt existed. The SJC denied the specifications, holding that BCO 31-2 gives the investigating court great discretion over procedure and timing and that the record did not show clear error; related complainants lacked standing.

artifacts.synopsis: TE James Thornton complained that Westminster Presbytery erred by declining to place a valid call from Memorial PCA into his hands and simultaneously invoking BCO 34-10 to begin divestiture proceedings. The SJC sustained the complaint, holding that the administrative remedy of BCO 34-10 cannot be invoked when a call is already in the presbytery's possession, and that presbytery's refusal lacked objective, justifiable grounds required for appellate review.

artifacts.title: Whether presbytery may investigate before proceeding to trial
artifacts.disposition: advice given — BCO 31-2 permits investigation before adjudication; amendments recommended

matches.evidence: BCO 31-2 permits a presbytery to investigate and determine strong presumption of guilt before adjudication; the CCB recommended amendments to BCO 31, 32, and 34 to clarify.

artifacts.title: Clarifying What Triggers a Required Investigative Inquiry Under BCO 31-2

matches.evidence: The CCB found Pacific Northwest Presbytery's overture clarifying investigation triggers not in conflict, though a dissent warned it could mandate inquiry even on slight grounds.
